pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that (1 mark)
   A. names a person, animal, place or thing
   B. describes a colour only
   C. shows an action
   D. joins two sentences

2. A word bank is (1 mark)
   A. a place for money
   B. a type of song
   C. a kind of poem
   D. a class list of useful words on one theme

3. A sentence should end with a (1 mark)
   A. full stop
   B. comma
   C. drawing
   D. capital letter

4. What is intonation? (1 mark)
   A. The size of letters
   B. The number of words
   C. The spelling of words
   D. The rise and fall of the voice

5. What should you do to check the punctuation in your paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. Read it aloud and listen for natural pauses
   B. Tear it
   C. Cover it
   D. Write it again without looking

6. Why should you look back at the dialogue when answering questions? (1 mark)
   A. To waste time
   B. To copy a friend
   C. To hide the page
   D. To find accurate answers

7. What is a tongue twister? (1 mark)
   A. A silent poem
   B. A phrase that is hard to say fast
   C. A very long word
   D. A kind of drum

8. What does Many hands make light work mean? (1 mark)
   A. Work is always easy
   B. Nobody should help
   C. Hands are light
   D. Work is easier when people share it

9. What is a reading club? (1 mark)
   A. A group that sells books
   B. A choir
   C. A group that meets to share and discuss books
   D. A team for running

10. What does Honesty is the best policy teach? (1 mark)
   A. Truth is unimportant
   B. Lying is fine
   C. Telling the truth is the wisest choice
   D. Only rich people are honest

11. Which is a good way to check a proverb's meaning? (1 mark)
   A. Ask an elder or teacher
   B. Ignore it
   C. Cover it
   D. Guess forever

12. What kind of word is when in When I arrived, the shop was closed? (1 mark)
   A. A noun
   B. A conjunction
   C. An adjective
   D. A number

13. What does a conjunction do? (1 mark)
   A. Describes a colour
   B. Joins words or sentences
   C. Names a thing
   D. Shows a feeling

14. What is the language train game? (1 mark)
   A. A reading test
   B. Pupils build a story with sentences beginning with when
   C. A game with real trains
   D. A running race

15. What should you keep in mind when scanning? (1 mark)
   A. A song
   B. What you are looking for
   C. A poem
   D. Nothing

16. What is animal welfare? (1 mark)
   A. Taking good care of animals so they are healthy and safe
   B. Ignoring animals
   C. Hunting animals
   D. Selling animals only

17. Which is a good tip for reciting? (1 mark)
   A. Look at the floor and mumble
   B. Cover your face
   C. Look at the audience and speak clearly
   D. Speak very fast

18. What is creative writing? (1 mark)
   A. Writing a list of names
   B. Writing only numbers
   C. Using imagination to write stories, poems and other pieces
   D. Copying a text exactly

19. Which interjection shows disgust? (1 mark)
   A. Yuck
   B. Hurray
   C. Aha
   D. Bravo

20. What is leisure time? (1 mark)
   A. Free time when you are not working or in class
   B. Exam time
   C. Sleeping time
   D. Lesson time

21. What should a dialogue about leisure show? (1 mark)
   A. Good values such as responsibility
   B. Rudeness
   C. Bad habits
   D. Unkindness

22. Which word in an advert may be used to persuade? (1 mark)
   A. door
   B. best
   C. table
   D. paper

23. What is news? (1 mark)
   A. Information about recent events
   B. Old stories only
   C. Songs
   D. Riddles

24. Why should you write true information on a form? (1 mark)
   A. Nobody reads forms
   B. Forms are records and false information causes problems
   C. False answers are best
   D. It is a game

25. What is rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. The title
   B. The ink
   C. The beat or flow when a poem is read aloud
   D. The page number

26. Does every poem have to rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. Only long poems
   B. Only short poems
   C. Yes, always
   D. No

27. What is a line in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. One row of words
   B. A whole page
   C. A stanza
   D. A book

28. Which word helps to show the order of steps? (1 mark)
   A. Table
   B. Finally
   C. Green
   D. Yesterday

29. Why should instruction charts use large clear letters? (1 mark)
   A. To make them heavy
   B. To use more ink
   C. To hide meaning
   D. So people can read them from a distance

30. What is the treasure hunt game used for? (1 mark)
   A. Sleeping
   B. Learning to sing
   C. Practising following instructions
   D. Drawing maps only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Name three parts of a simple form. (3 marks)

32. Plan a story that uses the proverb Many hands make light work. Give the title, characters, problem and ending. (4 marks)

33. Describe how to read a passage with interjections aloud. (4 marks)

34. Give three uses of capital letters in English. (3 marks)

35. Explain how the language train game is played. (4 marks)

36. Explain why leaders are important and why people should obey fair leaders. Give two examples of leaders in a community. (5 marks)

37. Explain how you would perform a choral poem with your class. Include voice, pace and non-verbal cues. (5 marks)

38. Make an instruction chart of five steps for keeping the class clean. Include a title and start each step with a verb. (5 marks)

39. List three tips for reciting a poem well. (3 marks)

40. Add capital letters, commas and full stops: on friday we bought rice beans and flour (3 marks)

41. Explain the steps of organising a class debate. (4 marks)

42. Write the four parts of a telephone conversation and give a short example of one. (4 marks)

43. List three ways of taking good care of a domestic animal. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — names a person, animal, place or thing
   Nouns are naming words.

2. D — a class list of useful words on one theme
   A vocabulary bank collects words by topic.

3. A — full stop
   A statement ends with a full stop.

4. D — The rise and fall of the voice
   Intonation is voice movement.

5. A — Read it aloud and listen for natural pauses
   Reading aloud helps find where pauses and stops belong.

6. D — To find accurate answers
   Answers should come from the text.

7. B — A phrase that is hard to say fast
   Tongue twisters train clear speech.

8. D — Work is easier when people share it
   It is a proverb about working together.

9. C — A group that meets to share and discuss books
   A reading club shares books and reading.

10. C — Telling the truth is the wisest choice
   It praises honesty.

11. A — Ask an elder or teacher
   Elders can explain the meaning.

12. B — A conjunction
   When joins two ideas by time.

13. B — Joins words or sentences
   Conjunctions are joining words.

14. B — Pupils build a story with sentences beginning with when
   Each pupil adds a when sentence.

15. B — What you are looking for
   Scanning needs a target.

16. A — Taking good care of animals so they are healthy and safe
   Welfare means care for animals' well-being.

17. C — Look at the audience and speak clearly
   Eye contact and clarity help.

18. C — Using imagination to write stories, poems and other pieces
   Creative writing is imaginative.

19. A — Yuck
   Yuck shows disgust.

20. A — Free time when you are not working or in class
   Leisure is free time.

21. A — Good values such as responsibility
   Dialogues can teach values.

22. B — best
   Words such as best persuade people to buy.

23. A — Information about recent events
   News reports what has happened.

24. B — Forms are records and false information causes problems
   Honest answers are important.

25. C — The beat or flow when a poem is read aloud
   Rhythm is the pattern of sounds.

26. D — No
   Some poems do not rhyme.

27. A — One row of words
   Poems are written in lines.

28. B — Finally
   Finally shows the last step.

29. D — So people can read them from a distance
   Clarity helps readers.

30. C — Practising following instructions
   Each note gives the next instruction.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, instructions, fields, signature, date.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any suitable plan, for example Title: The Clean Compound. Characters: pupils. Problem: a dirty compound. Ending: everyone helps and it is clean quickly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, find the interjections, decide the feeling of each, read each with the right voice, and keep a steady pace.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: The first word of a sentence, names of people and places, the word I, days and months (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each use.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: A pupil starts with a sentence. Each next pupil continues the story with a sentence beginning with when until the story ends.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: Leaders guide, make decisions and keep order. Obeying fair leaders keeps peace and safety. Examples: chief, teacher, class monitor, elders.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for why leaders are important, two marks for obeying and one for examples.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: Learn the poem well, keep the same pace together, speak clearly with expression, use gestures and smiles as non-verbal cues, look at the audience and practise beforehand.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of five points.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: Title: How to keep our class clean. 1. Sweep the floor. 2. Wipe the desks. 3. Put waste in the bin. 4. Wash your hands. 5. Close the windows.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the title, one mark for each of four steps that begin with verbs and are in order.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Learn it well, mark pauses and stressed words, speak clearly, look at the audience, keep a steady pace.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each tip.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: On Friday we bought rice, beans and flour.
   Working / marking points: One mark for capitals, one mark for the commas, one for the full stop.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a motion, form two teams, plan reasons, take turns to speak for about a minute each, listeners note points, the class votes.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Greet; say who you are and why you called; talk and listen; say goodbye. Example: Good afternoon, this is Neema speaking.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part and one mark for an example, with 4 marks maximum.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Give food and clean water, provide a shelter, take it to a veterinary doctor when sick, do not overload it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.
